problem_statement.title: [Bug]: JSON-RPC client ignores the JSON-RPC error body when the HTTP status is not 2xx
problem_statement.body:
### What happened?

`JsonRpcTransport` raises the mapped A2A error for a JSON-RPC error response only when the HTTP status is 2xx. If a server sends the same error body with a non-2xx status, the client raises a generic `A2AClientError("HTTP Error 500: ...")`. The JSON-RPC error code and the server's message are lost.

a2a-js does this. Errors raised outside its main handler (the user builder, the agent card lookup) that map to `-32603` are sent as HTTP 500 with a normal JSON-RPC error body ([json_rpc_handler.ts#L219-L220](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-js/blob/41335e66b6941db20065580782b909ff6e8476c0/src/server/express/json_rpc_handler.ts#L219-L220)). Section 9.5 of the spec defines the error object, not the HTTP status, so the client can't assume 200. `RestTransport` already reads the error body on non-2xx responses (`_handle_http_error`).

To reproduce on `main` (caab6a2):

```python
import asyncio

import httpx

from a2a.client.transports.jsonrpc import JsonRpcTransport
from a2a.types.a2a_pb2 import AgentCard, GetTaskRequest

BODY = {
    'jsonrpc': '2.0',
    'id': '1',
    'error': {'code': -32603, 'message': 'database connection lost'},
}


async def main(status: int) -> None:
    client = httpx.AsyncClient(
        transport=httpx.MockTransport(
            lambda request: httpx.Response(status, json=BODY)
        )
    )
    transport = JsonRpcTransport(client, AgentCard(), 'http://agent')
    try:
        await transport.get_task(GetTaskRequest(id='t1'))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f'HTTP {status}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}')


asyncio.run(main(200))
asyncio.run(main(500))
```

Expected: both calls raise `InternalError: database connection lost`.

Actual: the HTTP 500 call raises `A2AClientError: HTTP Error 500: ...`. `send_message_streaming` and `subscribe` behave the same way: a 404 whose body is a `-32001` error raises `A2AClientError` instead of `TaskNotFoundError`.

Root cause: `_send_request` and `_send_stream_request` pass no `status_error_handler` to the shared HTTP helpers ([jsonrpc.py#L319-L330](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-python/blob/caab6a252958b2218ea61c0cae772f0a5c159e2a/src/a2a/client/transports/jsonrpc.py#L319-L330), [jsonrpc.py#L368-L376](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-python/blob/caab6a252958b2218ea61c0cae772f0a5c159e2a/src/a2a/client/transports/jsonrpc.py#L368-L376)), so `handle_http_exceptions` raises without reading the body.

Proposed fix: give `JsonRpcTransport` a status error handler, like `RestTransport._handle_http_error`. If the body is a JSON-RPC error object, raise the mapped error. Otherwise keep the current `A2AClientError("HTTP Error ...")`, so HTML pages from proxies and other non-JSON-RPC bodies behave as today.

One behaviour change to flag: code that catches `A2AClientError` for these responses would get the mapped `A2AError` subclass instead (`InternalError` is not an `A2AClientError`). That's already what happens for the same body at HTTP 200, and what `RestTransport` does. `except A2AError` is unaffected.

I'm happy to open a PR for this.

### Relevant log output

```shell
HTTP 200: InternalError: database connection lost
HTTP 500: A2AClientError: HTTP Error 500: Server error '500 Internal Server Error' for url 'http://agent'
For more information check: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/500
```

problem_statement.title: SqlCatalog: accept an existing SQLAlchemy Engine
problem_statement.body:
### Feature Request / Improvement

`SqlCatalog.__init__` always builds its own engine from the `uri` property (`create_engine(uri, echo=..., pool_pre_ping=...)`). Since 0.12.0 it also runs `_init_catalog()` in the constructor, which queries the database to choose between the v0 and v1 catalog schema.

An application that already owns a configured `Engine` can't hand it to the catalog. Today it has to construct the catalog from a URI and then replace `catalog.engine`. With 0.12 the constructor's probe has already run by then, on the engine PyIceberg built.

That engine lacks what the application set on its own: a pool class and size, `connect_args` (an `ssl.SSLContext` for `sslmode=verify-full`, `application_name`, `statement_timeout`), a psycopg2 wait callback, and event listeners. Two failure modes follow:

- If the URI carries no password, because the application keeps secrets out of `catalog.properties`, the probe fails to authenticate. PyIceberg then reads the tables as absent and picks v1, whatever the real schema is.
- If the database requires TLS settings that only exist in code (an SSL context), the probe's connection is refused.

The probe also opens a connection in the constructor. An asyncio application has to remember to build the catalog off its event loop.

### Proposal

Accept an engine, for example `SqlCatalog(name, engine=engine, **properties)`, or a `SqlCatalog.from_engine(name, engine, **properties)` classmethod. When an engine is given, `uri` becomes optional and `_init_catalog()` runs on that engine. The `uri` property can still be set for display.

Example:

```python
engine = create_engine(url, connect_args={"sslcontext": context}, poolclass=QueuePool, pool_size=1)
catalog = SqlCatalog("default", engine=engine, warehouse="s3://bucket/prefix")
```

### Workaround we use

We subclass `SqlCatalog` and override `_init_catalog` with a no-op during `super().__init__`. We then set `self.engine` to our engine and call `SqlCatalog._init_catalog(self)` ourselves. This depends on a private method, which is why we'd like a supported way.

I can open a pull request for this.

problem_statement.title: embeddings: lone UTF-16 surrogate in input returns 500
problem_statement.body:
## What happens

`POST /v1/embeddings` returns **500** when an input string contains a lone UTF-16 surrogate, for example text extracted from a PDF by pdf.js and sent as JSON (`"\ud800"`). The tokenizer raises and the route turns it into a 500:

```
ERROR:rapid_mlx.routes.embeddings:Embedding generation failed: TextEncodeInput must be Union[TextInputSequence, Tuple[InputSequence, InputSequence]]
INFO:     127.0.0.1:52473 - "POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
```

One bad character in one input fails the whole batch.

## Repro (1.0.3)

```bash
rapid-mlx serve --embedding-model embeddinggemma-2-4bit --port 8466
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8466/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embeddinggemma-2-4bit","input":["ok","\ud800 lone"]}'
# 500
```

`["ok"]` returns 200 and `[]` returns 400, as expected.

## Expected

Either replace lone surrogates with U+FFFD before tokenizing (what OpenAI-compatible clients effectively get from servers that decode with `errors="replace"`), or return a 400 that names the offending input index. Not a 500.

Found while running a local research app that embeds PDF text; the client now sanitizes, but other clients will hit this.

problem_statement.title: [Bug] QQ group messages silently dropped on 2.2.2
problem_statement.body:
# [Bug] QQ group messages silently dropped on 2.2.2 — gateway dispatches `GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE`, but `_MESSAGE_EVENT_SPECS` only knows `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`

## Environment
- QwenPaw **2.2.2** (upgraded from 2.2.1, agentscope 2.0.10)
- Channel: QQ official bot, **group** chat
- Linux

## Symptom
After upgrading 2.2.1 → 2.2.2, the bot stops receiving **group** messages: @-mentioning the bot in a group produces no reply at all. Direct messages (`C2C_MESSAGE_CREATE`) keep working, and sending messages *to* the same group works fine. Reconnecting the WebSocket and fully restarting the app do not help — both connections reach `READY`, and no group event is ever logged.

## Root cause
A temporary log line in the gateway dispatch handler showed the event types actually dispatched:

```
dispatch seen t=READY s=1
dispatch seen t=GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE s=2 keys=['author','content','group_id','group_openid','id','message_scene','message_type','timestamp']
```

`_MESSAGE_EVENT_SPECS` in `qwenpaw/app/channels/qq/channel.py` registers only:

- `C2C_MESSAGE_CREATE`
- `AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`
- `DIRECT_MESSAGE_CREATE`
- `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`

`GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE` is missing, so `_handle_msg_event()` hits `spec is None` and returns silently — group messages are dropped with no log line, which makes this hard to diagnose.

## Fix that worked locally
```python
"GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE": _MessageEventSpec(
    message_type="group",
    sender_keys=("member_openid", "id"),
    extra_meta_keys=("group_openid",),
),
```

Group messages are delivered again after adding this entry.

## Notes
- Not caused by the replayed-event guard from #8006 — no "duplicate dispatch" warnings were logged while the issue was happening.
- Probably worth keeping **both** `GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE` and `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE` registered, since the dispatched name may depend on bot type/permissions.

+def _validate_encoding_config(
+    config: ConfigMappingType, logging_reference: str
+) -> None:
+    """Validate that the core ``encoding`` is ``autodetect`` or a text encoding.
+
+    Otherwise the value is only used when ``open()`` reads each file, where an
+    unknown codec crashes the run with an uncaught ``LookupError``.

+    core_section = config.get("core", {})
+    if not core_section:

problem_statement.title: Unknown `encoding` crashes with LookupError traceback instead of a config error
problem_statement.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the issues and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

An unknown `encoding` value, given with `--encoding` or set in a config file, isn't validated. It is only used when each file is opened, where Python raises `LookupError` and the run crashes with a traceback.

### Expected Behaviour

A clean config error and exit code 2, like other invalid core values (for example `runaway_limit = x`):

```
Error loading config: Config file '...' set an invalid value for `encoding`: 'nope'. ...
```

### Observed Behaviour

```
$ sqlfluff lint a.sql --dialect ansi --encoding nope
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../sqlfluff/core/linter/linter.py", line 159, in load_raw_file_and_config
    with open(fname, encoding=encoding, errors="backslashreplace") as target_file:
LookupError: unknown encoding: nope
```

The same traceback appears with `encoding = nope` in `.sqlfluff`.

### How to reproduce

```
printf 'select a from b\n' > a.sql
sqlfluff lint a.sql --dialect ansi --encoding nope
```

### Dialect

Any (ansi used above).

### Version

sqlfluff 4.5.0 (`main` at 56a22f9), Python 3.13.3, macOS.

### Configuration

None needed for `--encoding`. For the config file variant:

```ini
[sqlfluff]
dialect = ansi
encoding = nope
```

### Are you willing to work on and submit a PR to address the issue?

- [x] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

problem_statement.title: Provide a TestCase subclass/mixin for running in a temp dir
problem_statement.body:
We have a lot of tests that have a pattern lik
```python
class TestThing(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.td = TemporaryDirectoryChanger()
        self.td.__enter__()
    def tearDown(self):
        self.td.__exit__(None, None, None)
```

problem_statement.title: ST01 silently deletes a comment inside a redundant ELSE NULL clause on autofix
problem_statement.body:
## Summary

`ST01` (`structure.else_null`) removes a redundant `ELSE NULL` clause from a `CASE` expression when autofixing. If that `ELSE NULL` clause contains a comment (e.g. `else /* keep default */ null`), the comment is a child of the deleted `else_clause` segment, so `sqlfluff fix` silently deletes the comment along with the clause — with no warning, and no way for the user to recover it afterwards.

**Impact: data-loss**

Entry point / who reaches it: any user running `sqlfluff fix` (or `lint --fix`) with `ST01`/`structure.else_null` enabled — it's in the default `all` rule group — on a `CASE` expression whose redundant `ELSE NULL` branch carries a comment.

Reproduction:
```sql
select
    case
        when name = 'cat' then 'meow'
        when name = 'dog' then 'woof'
        else /* keep default */ null
    end
from x
```
Before this fix, `sqlfluff fix --dialect ansi --rules ST01` on the above silently drops `else /* keep default */ null` entirely, including the comment — the user's annotation is gone with no diagnostic. There is no `--fix` output, log line, or lint message that mentions the comment at all.

## Root cause

`Rule_ST01._eval` (`src/sqlfluff/rules/structure/ST01.py`), on detecting a redundant `else null`, unconditionally emits `LintFix.delete(else_clause[0])` plus deletes of the leading whitespace — deleting the entire `else_clause` segment as one unit. A comment nested between the `ELSE` keyword and the `NULL` literal is a genuine child of that segment (not a sibling the rule already preserves), so it is deleted along with the redundant clause. Nothing in the rule inspects the clause's children for a comment before deleting it.

## Fix

Before deleting the clause, look for comment children of `else_clause`. If any are found, re-home them onto their own line immediately after the last `WHEN` clause (so they attach to the `CASE` expression the same way a comment placed there manually would), then delete the clause as before. Verified this can't leave an `else_clause` with no expression child for a case ST02 might also touch, since the whole clause is still deleted as a single unit either way — only the comment is relocated, not exempted from the clause deletion.

## Testing (negative control — reproduce by execution)

Added `redundant_else_null_preserves_comment` to `test/fixtures/rules/std_rule_cases/ST01.yml`.

With the production fix reverted (fixture kept), running the targeted test fails exactly this new case and nothing else:
```
$ pytest test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py -k ST01 -q
FAILED test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py::test__rule_test_case[ST01_redundant_else_null_preserves_comment]
1 failed, 5 passed, 2501 deselected in 3.15s
```
With the fix restored:
```
$ pytest test/rules/yaml_test_cases_test.py -k ST01 -q
......                                                                   [100%]
6 passed, 2501 deselected in 2.78s
```
The new case fails without the fix and passes with it; the other 5 pre-existing ST01 cases are unaffected in both directions. Also ran `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `yamllint -c .yamllint`, and `mypy -p sqlfluff.rules.structure.ST01` — all clean.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change was AI-assisted: an AI agent located the bug by reading `ST01.py` and its fixtures, proposed the initial diagnosis, and drafted the fix and regression test. I manually validated it before submitting: I independently re-read `Rule_ST01._eval`'s delete-the-whole-clause logic myself rather than trusting the diagnosis as given; I ran the reproduction SQL through `sqlfluff fix` myself and read the actual (comment-dropping) output; and I ran the full test suite (negative control, full ST0* family, ruff/yamllint/mypy) myself and read the results shown above rather than taking a report of them at face value.

Signed-off-by: Udaya Tejas <udayatejas2004@gmail.com>

problem_statement.title: AsyncGRPOTrainer hangs forever without an error when every group is dropped
problem_statement.body:
### Reproduction

```python
from datasets import load_dataset
from trl import AsyncGRPOConfig, AsyncGRPOTrainer

def constant_reward(completions, **kwargs):
    return [1.0] * len(completions)

# vLLM server serving trl-internal-testing/tiny-Qwen2ForCausalLM-2.5 on http://localhost:8000
trainer = AsyncGRPOTrainer(
    model="trl-internal-testing/tiny-Qwen2ForCausalLM-2.5",
    reward_funcs=constant_reward,
    args=AsyncGRPOConfig(output_dir="out", per_device_train_batch_size=3, num_generations=3, max_completion_length=8, vllm_server_base_url="http://localhost:8000"),
    train_dataset=load_dataset("trl-internal-testing/zen", "conversational_prompt_only", split="train"),
)
trainer.train()
```

outputs, forever, with `trainer.state.global_step` staying at 0:

```
[RANK 0] waited 1.2s for sample (qsize=0)
[RANK 0] waited 1.2s for sample (qsize=0)
...
```

Every group has equal rewards, so it is dropped, and `RolloutQueueDataset.__iter__` skips its group id and waits for the next sample, with no limit:

https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/f27a906d3/trl/trainer/async_grpo_trainer.py#L2314-L2316

No step can complete, so the weights never change and every later group is dropped too. Rejecting every prompt of an epoch with `filter_prompt` raises instead.

### How did you hit this?

Investigating a CI hang:
- https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/8420

There, an fp16 test collapses the tiny model to one repeated token after 2 or 3 steps, and the run then hangs until the CI runner kills it after 4 hours. A user hits the same hang, with no error, once every group of their run has equal rewards: a collapsed policy, or prompts that all become too easy or too hard (e.g. 0/1 rewards). Since v1.17.0 (`trl.experimental`), stable since v1.18.0.

Reproduced on 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB with the transformers-backed stand-in vLLM server of the AsyncGRPO tests; with `str_length_reward` instead, the same run returns after 79 s.

- Python version: 3.13.9

- vLLM version: not installed

problem_statement.title: spec: shift with an absent per-entity offset reads x[t=0] (wrap) or 0 (edge=0) instead of no row
problem_statement.body:
> [!NOTE]
> The following content was generated by AI.

`shift(x, along=t, offset=lag, edge=...)` casts an absent `lag[e]` to int in `linopy/spec/operators.py` (`_gather_by_offset`, and the fill mask of `_gather_in_groups`). For that entity:

- `edge='wrap'`: every `t` reads `x[t=0]`.
- `edge=0`: the shifted term is 0, so the row survives.

Expected: where the offset is absent the shift is not defined, so the row is absent, like a `within=` member placed in no group.

```python
import pandas as pd
from linopy import Model

t = pd.Index([0, 1, 2, 3], name="t")
e = pd.Index(["a", "b"], name="e")
data = {"t": t, "e": e, "lag": pd.DataFrame({"e": ["a"], "lag": [1]})}  # no lag for e='b'
for edge in ["0", "'wrap'"]:
    spec = {
        "dimensions": {"t": {"dtype": "int", "ordered": True}, "e": {"dtype": "str"}},
        "parameters": {"lag": {"dims": ["e"], "dtype": "int", "missing": "absent"}},
        "variables": {"x": {"dims": ["t", "e"]}},
        "constraints": {
            "c": {
                "dims": ["t", "e"],
                "expression": f"x + shift(x, along=t, offset=lag, edge={edge}) >= 0",
            }
        },
    }
    m = Model.from_spec(spec, data)
    print(f"edge={edge}:", m.constraints["c"].sel(e="b"), sep="\n")
```

Output on master (ac3eaf7):

```
edge=0:
[0]: +1 x[b, 0] ≥ 0.0
[1]: +1 x[b, 1] ≥ 0.0
[2]: +1 x[b, 2] ≥ 0.0
[3]: +1 x[b, 3] ≥ 0.0
edge='wrap':
[0]: +1 x[b, 0] + 1 x[b, 0] ≥ 0.0
[1]: +1 x[b, 1] + 1 x[b, 0] ≥ 0.0
[2]: +1 x[b, 2] + 1 x[b, 0] ≥ 0.0
[3]: +1 x[b, 3] + 1 x[b, 0] ≥ 0.0
```

Expected: all four `e='b'` rows absent in both cases. Same for `sparse=True`, and for `edge=0` with `within=`.

problem_statement.title: FiniteVolume: harmonic face averaging of a bare gradient's factor under Division/Addition
problem_statement.body:
`FiniteVolume.process_binary_operators` averages a node-valued factor onto faces with the harmonic mean whenever the other child is a bare `pybamm.Gradient`, under **any** binary operator. #5856 added the opt-in `"harmonic flux coefficients"` option (default `False`): when it is on, a coefficient multiplying a signed sum of gradient terms also takes the harmonic mean, but only under `Multiplication`. #5856 left the bare-`Gradient` rule as it was, which leaves an inconsistency whether the option is on or off:

| expression | mean used for `w` |
|---|---|
| `grad(u) / w` | harmonic (bare-`Gradient` rule) |
| `(grad(u) - grad(v)) / w` | arithmetic |
| `w + grad(u)` | harmonic |

For a resistivity in a denominator, the distance-weighted **arithmetic** mean of `w` is the correct series value. The harmonic mean of `w` is only right when `w` is a conductance. Harmonic averaging under `Addition`/`Subtraction` has no physical meaning.

No built-in model uses `grad(u) / w` or `w ± grad(u)` with a node-valued `w`: an audit of the DFN family, MSMR and lead-acid found none. Changing the bare-`Gradient` rule could still move user models' results, which is why #5856 left it alone.

Proposal: restrict the harmonic mean to `Multiplication` for bare gradients too, and use the arithmetic mean for `Division` and for additive operators. Add a CHANGELOG note, since results for user models written this way would change.

`FiniteVolume2D` has the same bare-`Gradient` rule; that is being handled separately.

problem_statement.title: SSH Config with multi-path `Include hosts/*.conf hosts/*/*.conf` directive is ignored.
problem_statement.body:
## Describe the bug

Pyinfra does not parse `Include` directive with multiple paths, eg 

```sshconfig
# .ssh/config
Include hosts/*.conf hosts/*/*.conf
# swapping the order does not help, ie i dont think its simply reading the first path
# Include hosts/*/*.conf hosts/*.conf 
```

Per `OpenSSH_10.5p1, OpenSSL 3.6.4 25 Aug 2026`, "Include  the specified configuration file(s).  *Multiple pathnames may be specified*...`, so I believe this is valid syntax, SSH functions as expected.

```
Include
             Include  the specified configuration file(s).  Multiple pathnames may be specified and each pathname may
             contain [glob(7)](man:glob(7)) wildcards, tokens as described in the “TOKENS” section,  environment  variables  as  de‐
             scribed  in  the “ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES” section and, for user configurations, shell-like ‘~’ references
             to user home directories.  Wildcards will be expanded and processed in lexical order.  Files without ab‐
             solute paths are assumed to be in ~/.ssh if included in a user configuration file  or  /etc/ssh  if  in‐
             cluded from the system configuration file.  Include directive may appear inside a Match or Host block to
             perform conditional inclusion.
```

## Workaround

Give each path in its own `Include` directive,

```
# .ssh/config
Include hosts/*.conf
Include hosts/*/*.conf
```

## To Reproduce

Create a structure like:

```
.ssh/
  config
  hosts/
    site_a.conf
    site_b/
       site_b.conf
```

Where the site config is something that wont succeed without reading the config (eg it needs a specific port or internal ip, etc.)

```
Host site_b.noresolve
  Hostname site_b.com
  ...
```

Then

```
uv pyinfra inventory/site_b.py myop
```

where the inventory just defines "site_b.noresolve" as the target.


## Expected behavior

Pyinfra connects and acts as normal.

## Meta
```
   System: Linux
      Platform: Linux-7.2.7-arch1-1-x86_64-with-glibc2.44
      Release: 7.2.7-arch1-1
      Machine: x86_64
    pyinfra: v3.10.0
      click: v8.3.1
      distro: v1.9.0
      gevent: v25.9.1
      jinja2: v3.1.6
      packaging: v26.0
      paramiko: v3.5.1
      pydantic: v2.12.5
      python-dateutil: v2.9.0.post0
      typeguard: v4.4.4
      types-paramiko: v4.0.0.20260518
      typing-extensions: v4.15.0
    Executable: /home/.../.venv/bin/pyinfra
```
    Python: 3.14.7 (CPython, GCC 16.1.1 20260728)
+ How was pyinfra installed (source/pip)? *uv*

problem_statement.title: [Bug]: Experiment steps with long drive cycles that differ only in the middle are treated as the same step
problem_statement.body:
### PyBaMM Version

main

### Python Version

3.14

### Describe the bug

Steps are identified by text: `Experiment.process_steps` keys the processed steps on `repr(step)`, and `BaseStep.__eq__`, `__hash__` and `basic_repr` compare `hash_args`, a string built from the step's value. For a drive cycle, that string is the numpy repr of the array, which numpy shortens to `...` above 1000 entries (500 rows for a 2-column drive cycle).

Two drive cycles with the same first and last three rows therefore give the same step. `Experiment` replaces the second with a copy of the first, so the experiment runs the first drive cycle twice, with no error or warning. Real drive cycles are usually much longer than 500 rows.

This is the same kind of collision as #5529, which added the class name to the key but kept comparing text.

### Steps to Reproduce


```python
import numpy as np
import pybamm

# Two drive cycles that differ only at t = 500 s
t = np.linspace(0, 1000, 2001)
drive_cycle_1 = np.column_stack([t, np.ones_like(t)])
drive_cycle_2 = drive_cycle_1.copy()
drive_cycle_2[1000, 1] = 5

step_1 = pybamm.step.current(drive_cycle_1)
step_2 = pybamm.step.current(drive_cycle_2)
print(step_1 == step_2)  # True

experiment = pybamm.Experiment([step_1, step_2])
print(len(experiment.unique_steps))  # 1

sim = pybamm.Simulation(pybamm.lithium_ion.SPM(), experiment=experiment)
solution = sim.solve()
for cycle in solution.cycles:
    print(cycle["Current [A]"](cycle.t[0] + 500))
# 1.0 for both steps, but the second drive cycle is 5 A at t = 500 s
```

The result is the same with `experiment_model_mode="unified"`.

### Relevant log output

```shell
True
1
1.0
1.0
```

problem_statement.title: Automatic Mod evaluation with Floats
problem_statement.body:
Mod has strange automatic evaluation with Float arguments:

```
>>> Mod(x, 1.0)
Mod(1.0*x, 1)
>>> Mod(x, 3.3)
Mod(1.0*x, 3.3)
>>> Mod(x, 0.5)
0.5*(Mod(2*x, 1))
```

It's not clear to me that any of these rewrites are necessary.

 def ref_matches(ref, pattern, is_consumer):
     if not ref or not str(ref):
         assert is_consumer
-        ref = RecipeReference.loads("*/*")  # FIXME: ugly
+        # An unnamed consumer (conanfile.txt, conanfile.py without name, test_package, virtual
+        # --requires) is not a recipe reference. Patterns restricted to recipes without
+        # user/channel ("*@") must not select it, so a generic "*@:xxx" can define the
+        # "third-party" packages without forcing it into the consumer. The consumer can still be
+        # selected explicitly with "&" or "&@"
+        selector = pattern.lstrip("!~")
+        no_user_channel = selector.endswith("@")
+        if no_user_channel and not selector.startswith("&"):
+            ref = RecipeReference.loads("*/*@*/*")
+        else:
+            ref = RecipeReference.loads("*/*")
     return ref.matches(pattern, is_consumer=is_consumer)

+"""
+Scenario from https://github.com/conan-io/conan/issues/20527
+
+Build every third-party dependency (those without user/channel, e.g. ConanCenter recipes) in
+Release, while our own packages (with user/channel) and the "consumer" follow the requested
+``build_type``.
+
+The natural way to express it is a ``*@:build_type=Release`` settings pattern, but ``*@`` also
+matches the consumer (a consumer has no user/channel), so the consumer is silently forced to
+Release too. The ``&`` consumer pattern can only assign a fixed value, it cannot say "follow the
+requested one", and there is no way to exclude the consumer from a ``*@`` pattern.
+
+The most problematic case is ``conan create``, where several things are "the consumer": the
+package being created and the ``test_package`` conanfile. With ``--user/--channel`` the created
+package follows the requested ``build_type``, but the ``test_package`` (no user/channel) does not,
+so a Debug package is tested with a Release ``test_package``.
+"""
+import json
+import textwrap
+
+import pytest
+
+from conan.test.assets.genconanfile import GenConanfile
+from conan.test.utils.tools import TestClient
+
+
+def _build_types(client):
+    """ {name: build_type} of the nodes of the graph (json output) of the last client run.
+    The root node (consumer or test_package) has no name and it is reported as "root" """
+    nodes = json.loads(client.stdout)["graph"]["nodes"].values()
+    return {n["name"] or "root": n["settings"]["build_type"] for n in nodes}
+
+
+@pytest.fixture()

problem_statement.title: [feature] Support excluding the consumer from *@ settings patterns
problem_statement.body:
### What is your suggestion?

A common setup builds every third-party dependency in Release while the user's own code follows the requested `build_type`. Debug builds of a large dependency graph then stay fast, binary-cache hits go up, and only the code you're actually debugging is built in Debug.

We'd like:
  - every dependency without user/channel (for example ConanCenter recipes, which have no user/channel) in Release, including new ones added to the graph later
  - our own packages (with a user/channel, e.g. `@company/stable`) to follow the requested `build_type`
  - the consumer (a local `conanfile.py`, `--requires`, the package of `conan create` and its test_package) to follow the requested `build_type`

### Have you read the CONTRIBUTING guide?

- [ ] I've read the CONTRIBUTING guide

     """
     Gets a jinja2 ``Template`` object for the input filename or string, with caching
     based on the filename of the template, or the SHA1 of the input string.
+
+    If a custom ``loader`` is supplied and ``filename_or_io`` is a template name
+    that does not exist as a local path, the loader searches for that name
+    (so a ``FileSystemLoader`` search path is honoured). Existing file paths
+    and IO objects are still read directly and compiled with ``from_string``.
     """
     if jinja_env_kwargs is None:
         jinja_env_kwargs = {}
+    else:
+        # Copy so popping the default loader cannot mutate the caller's dict.
+        jinja_env_kwargs = dict(jinja_env_kwargs)
+
+    loader = jinja_env_kwargs.get("loader")
+    if (
+        loader is not None
+        and isinstance(filename_or_io, str)
+        and not os.path.isfile(filename_or_io)
+    ):
+        cache_key = f"loader:{id(loader)}:{filename_or_io}"

+            return TEMPLATES[cache_key]

+            undefined=StrictUndefined,
+            keep_trailing_newline=True,
+            **jinja_env_kwargs,
+        ).get_template(filename_or_io)
+        TEMPLATES[cache_key] = template
+        return template

+            template = get_template(existing, {"loader": jinja2.FileSystemLoader([search])})

problem_statement.title: Template path made absolute, prevents loader from searching template
problem_statement.body:
## Describe the bug
A Jinja2 template loader's job is to load a template. One of the concepts used is the search path, i.e. the loader looks for a template by its basename in a series of locations, and returns the first found.

Pyinfra's `files.template` takes a `jinja2_env_args` dict and initialises the Jinja2 environment with a user-supplied loader, if provided.

However, `pyinfra.operations.files.template` and `pyinfra.api.util.get_template` actually do more, and in doing so, renders any user-supplied loader ineffective, for two reasons:

1. `files.template` prepends the state's working directory to the user provided template name, turning the template name into an absolute path. This means that any custom `FilesystemLoader` with a search path will always fail: e.g. "TemplateNotFound: '/home/madduck/sa/infra/motd.j2' not found in search paths: '/home/madduck/sa/infra/templates', '/home/madduck/sa/infra/src/mdinfra/templates'". It is iterating the search paths, but unable to look for the template `motd.j2`, because the absolute path is being passed.
2. Furthermore, instead of letting the loader load the template, `api.util.get_template` actually `read()`'s the entire template into memory and calls `jinja2.Environment.from_string` instead, thereby circumventing the entire template search logic.

## To Reproduce

```Python
import jinja2

from pyinfra.api.util import get_template

loader = jinja2.FileSystemLoader(["/etc", "/tmp"])

get_template("fstab", {"loader": loader})
```
This produces:

```sh
% python3 test.py                                                                                                                   Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/madduck/code/pyinfra/test.py", line 7, in <module>
    get_template("fstab", {"loader": loader})
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/madduck/code/pyinfra/src/pyinfra/api/util.py", line 164, in get_template
    with file_data as file_io:
         ^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/madduck/code/pyinfra/src/pyinfra/api/util.py", line 386, in __enter__
    file_io = open(self.filename_or_io, self.mode)
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'fstab'
```

## Expected behavior
If I pass a loader with a search path, I expect the template to be searched in order of this search path, and the first instance found to be used.

Without a custom loader, I expect the template to be resolved relatively to the working directory, unless passed as an absolute path.

## Suggested fix
I understand that changing this will break existing templates. Therefore, maybe a viable path forward could be to deprecate the `src` field/argument of `operations.files.template` and instead introduce a new `name` field. Alternatively, make `src` be the field to specify a template to use, documenting that the loader is circumvented (possibly conflicting/raising a `RuntimeError` when a loader with a search path is passed as well as `src`), and conflict with `name` as well.

## Additional

`api.util.get_template` implements poor-man's caching on templates it loads into memory, even though jinja2's `FilesystemLoader` already implements caching. By properly using the loader, this code could be reduced.

## Meta

problem_statement.title: Make Engine.is_series_like a real type guard
problem_statement.body:
## Problem

`graphistry/Engine.py::is_series_like` is the typed helper the docs and the `dynamic-attr` hygiene check point people to, but it is implemented as `hasattr(s, "dropna") or is_polars_series(s)` and returns a plain `bool`. So:

- mypy gets no narrowing from it; call sites still need ignores or stay untyped.
- It is true for anything with `.dropna`, including a DataFrame.
- The duck-typed probe is centralised, not removed.

## Expected

- `is_series_like` returns a `TypeGuard` for the engine Series union and decides by type (pandas `isinstance`, the existing cuDF and Polars guards), not by attribute probing.
- Every existing caller is checked: any that relies on a DataFrame or another non-Series passing gets its own explicit check.
- No behaviour change on pandas, cuDF, Polars and polars-gpu test lanes; mypy count does not rise.

problem_statement.title: spec: `otherwise` is checked where a case already applies
problem_statement.body:
> [!NOTE]
> The following content was generated by AI.

### Version Checks

- [x] exists on `master` (127a61c)

### Issue Description

`Model.from_spec` checks the value of `otherwise:` at coordinates that a case already claims. A case that guards bad data, such as `cap == inf`, therefore can't stop the refusal.

- mathspec: `otherwise` is "the value at every coordinate that no case claims" ([named.md](https://github.com/energy-models/mathspec/blob/main/docs/reference/language/named.md#cases))
- `_evaluated` (`linopy/spec/evaluator.py`, the `ms.Cases` branch) evaluates each region's value on all rows, then masks it with `_in_region`. The finiteness check fires during that first evaluation. `refuse_holes` already limits itself to the region.
- found while building PyPSA from a spec: an unrated component (`p_nom = inf`) needs a guard like this; PyPSA's spec now repeats the guard in every `where:` instead.

### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr
from linopy import Model

spec = {
    "dimensions": {"t": {"dtype": "int"}},
    "parameters": {"cap": {"dims": ["t"]}, "pu": {"dims": ["t"]}},
    "variables": {"x": {"dims": ["t"], "bounds": {"lower": 0, "upper": 1}}},
    "expressions": {
        "used": {
            "dims": ["t"],
            "cases": {"unrated": {"when": "cap == inf", "expression": "1"}},
            "otherwise": "cap * pu",
        }
    },
    "constraints": {"limit": {"dims": ["t"], "expression": "x <= used"}},
    "objective": {"sense": "maximize", "expression": "sum(x, over=t)"},
}
```

problem_statement.title: pixel_array raises a bare StopIteration when encapsulated Pixel Data has fewer frames than Number of Frames
problem_statement.body:
**Describe the issue**

If encapsulated *Pixel Data* contains fewer frames than *Number of Frames* says, `Dataset.pixel_array` (and `Decoder.as_array()` / `as_buffer()`) raises a bare `StopIteration` with no message. It comes from `next(frame_generator)` in `_as_array_encapsulated` and `_as_buffer_encapsulated`, which call `next()` once per expected frame.

A bare `StopIteration` is worse than an ordinary error, because Python treats it as "no more items":

- Inside `map()`, it ends the iteration silently. Mapping over four datasets where the second one is short returns one result and no error. The short dataset and the two good ones after it are dropped.
- Inside a generator, it turns into `RuntimeError: generator raised StopIteration`, which doesn't say what's wrong with the file.

The opposite case (more frames than *Number of Frames*) already gets a clear warning and the `allow_excess_frames` option. Fewer frames isn't handled.

I found this while fuzzing `dcmread` and `pixel_array` with mutated copies of the test files (about 1.6M inputs). Otherwise the reader held up well: no hangs, no runaway memory use, no recursion errors.

**Steps to reproduce**

```python
from pydicom import dcmread
from pydicom.data import get_testdata_file

path = get_testdata_file("emri_small_RLE.dcm")  # RLE Lossless, 10 frames

def load(short):
    ds = dcmread(path)
    if short:
        ds.NumberOfFrames = ds.NumberOfFrames + 1  # one more than is encoded
    return ds.pixel_array.shape

try:
    load(True)
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, repr(e))       # StopIteration StopIteration()

print(list(map(load, [False, True, False, False])))
# [(10, 64, 64)]  -- one result, no error
```

Traceback for the direct call:

```
  File ".../pydicom/pixels/utils.py", line 1430, in pixel_array
    return decoder.as_array(
  File ".../pydicom/pixels/decoders/base.py", line 1000, in as_array
    arr = runner.reshape(func(runner, index), as_frame=as_frame)
  File ".../pydicom/pixels/decoders/base.py", line 1067, in _as_array_encapsulated
    frame = next(frame_generator)
StopIteration
```

I'd expect a `ValueError` naming the mismatch, in the same style as the excess-frames warning. I have a fix with tests and can open a PR.

**Environment** (`python -m pydicom.env_info`, released 3.0.2; also reproduced on main at 60cebd0)

```
module       | version
------       | -------
platform     | macOS-26.6.2-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O
Python       | 3.14.7
pydicom      | 3.0.2
numpy        | 2.5.3
```

problem_statement.title: [REQ] Replace hard-coded MuJoCo joint-type constants in the SolverMuJoCo kernels with an enum
problem_statement.body:
### Description

`newton/_src/solvers/mujoco/kernels.py` compares MuJoCo joint types against integer literals with a comment naming the constant, for example `jnt_type[jnt] == 0  # mjJNT_FREE` and `jnt_type[mjc_jnt] >= 2  # mjJNT_SLIDE or mjJNT_HINGE`, and the same in `update_jnt_reference_kernel` and `update_joint_transforms_kernel`. Replace the literals with a named enum. No behavior change.

### Motivation / Use Case

Raised in review of #5312 (https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/pull/5312#discussion_r4584359624): the literals are hard to read and nothing checks them against MuJoCo's values.

### Alternatives Considered

`kernels.py` is loaded without MuJoCo installed (MJCF/USD import pulls in `SolverMuJoCo`, and `mujoco`/`mujoco-warp` are only in the `sim` extra), and `mujoco.mjtJoint` is a pybind11 enum that Warp kernels cannot parse. That leaves two options:

1. A private `IntEnum` mirror of `mjtJoint` in `newton/_src/solvers/mujoco/enums.py`, pinned against `mujoco.mjtJoint` by a test, as `TestActuatorTypes` does for the actuator-type mirrors. The name must not clash with Newton's `JointType`, which `kernels.py` already imports.
2. `mujoco_warp.JointType`, which is an `IntEnum` and works in kernels, with the affected kernels created lazily after the MuJoCo import, as `_import_contact_force_fn` does today.

problem_statement.title: An aliased import with an opening-line comment goes past line_length, and isort and black keep rewrapping it
problem_statement.body:
With `--profile black`, isort and black never agree on an aliased import that only fits on one line without its `# noqa` comment. On main (1060ab4) and on 9.0.2, with black 26.10.1:

```console
$ cat example.py
from some.package.with_a_rather_long_module_name import (
    SomeLongClassName as alias,  # noqa: N813
)
$ isort --profile black example.py
Fixing /tmp/demo/example.py
$ cat example.py
from some.package.with_a_rather_long_module_name import (  # noqa: N813
    SomeLongClassName as alias,
)
$ isort --profile black example.py
Fixing /tmp/demo/example.py
$ cat example.py
from some.package.with_a_rather_long_module_name import SomeLongClassName as alias  # noqa: N813
$ black -q example.py
$ cat example.py
from some.package.with_a_rather_long_module_name import (
    SomeLongClassName as alias,
)  # noqa: N813
$ isort --profile black example.py
Fixing /tmp/demo/example.py
$ cat example.py
from some.package.with_a_rather_long_module_name import SomeLongClassName as alias  # noqa: N813
```

The second isort run writes a 96-character line, past the profile's line length of 88. From then on black wraps it and isort joins it back on every run, so with both tools in pre-commit the file is modified every time. 10.0.0b1 does the same, while 8.0.1 keeps the wrapped form from the first run on. It happens in real code too: on matplotlib's [backend_wxcairo.py](https://github.com/matplotlib/matplotlib/blob/e2256af2e75b4342ea943efe193e4dac3e3b5a67/lib/matplotlib/backends/backend_wxcairo.py#L5-L6), `isort --profile black` writes `from .backend_wx import NavigationToolbar2Wx as NavigationToolbar2WxCairo  # noqa: F401 # pylint: disable=W0611`, which is 111 characters long. Other opening-line comments also end up past `line_length`, although black leaves the joined line alone when the comment is a `# type: ignore`.

`_build_as_imports` wraps the import without the opening-line comment and adds the comment to the first line afterwards ([output.py#L373-L391](https://github.com/PyCQA/isort/blob/1060ab47708b7a7c907f30e1be56bf6b2647bd0e/isort/output.py#L373-L391)), so an import that fits on its own ends up past `line_length` once the comment is added. This came with 5349578a in #2491, which dropped the branch that wrapped this single-line case again with the comment included. A plain import in the same situation stays wrapped with the comment on the `(` line.

I have a fix with a regression test and will open a pull request for it.
